messages:
maria: FYI rack-12 (us-west1c) GPUs overheating — temps hitting 88-92°C and the scheduler has started evicting pods to reduce heat. Grafana: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/abcd/thermal?panelId=7

devon: @oncall did the pager fire? :fire:

sre-bot: Incident INC-2024-432 created by monitoring-bot — Rack thermal spike in us-west1c — P2 — https://inc.redwood.internal/INC-432

kai: Any pattern yet? binpack-induced hotspot or hardware fault? My guess: a bunch of small inference pods got packed on the same top-of-rack and heated it up.

anya: Looking at PDU & CRAC telemetry now. PDU current draw is high for rack-12, cooling damper looks low on that aisle. Tech team inbound ETA ~10m.

maria: I’m going to taint the nodes to stop new placements and soft-drain noncritical replicas to avoid more heat.

maria: ```bash
# labeling + taint to prevent new pods
kubectl label nodes rack-12-node1 rack=hot-12
kubectl taint nodes rack-12-node[1-4] gpu-hot=true:NoSchedule
# soft drain low-priority pods (short grace)
kubectl drain rack-12-node3 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=30
```

devon: Can we avoid a mass eviction cascade? last time backfills + preemptions thrashed the cluster for 20m.

kai: If the scheduler's binpack scoring is still high, it will compact tiny pods and recreate hotspots. Quick mitigation: temporarily reduce binpack weight, increase topologySpread weight for small pods.

maria: Proposed kube-scheduler score patch (canary in us-west1c):
```yaml
apiVersion: kubescheduler.config.k8s.io/v1
kind: KubeSchedulerConfiguration
profiles:
- schedulerName: default-scheduler
  plugins:
    score:
      enabled:
      - name: NodeResourcesFit
        weight: 1
      - name: BinPacking
        weight: 1   # lowered to reduce aggressive packing
      - name: TopologySpread
        weight: 6   # boosted to encourage rack spread
```

anya: Cooling team flipped the PDU to redundant feed; GPU temps falling — now ~72°C on affected nodes. Portable fans en route.

sre-bot: Alert rule updated: GPU_temp > 75C & packing_skew > 0.6 => page oncall. (Old page threshold was 80C.)

devon: Heads up: spreading will increase cross-rack network hops for KV cache and could raise inference p99 slightly. We'll mark latency-sensitive pools with affinity to keep them together when possible.

maria: Plan: mark latency-critical inference pools with nodeAffinity to prefer low-latency racks; leave bulk/batch inference as spreadable. Rolling the labels now.

kai: I’ll run the scheduler config canary in us-west1c only (no global restart). Watch pack/skew and reschedule churn for 10m before wider rollout.

maria: Current count: 6 evicted pods, 4 backfilled to warm-pool in neighboring racks, no SLO breaches yet. Keeping incident open until rack stabilizes. Thanks all :thermometer: :wrench:
